title: Role records for the consistency audit (profile/role-records.json)
description: The person's work history copied, exactly as written, from each source (CV, LinkedIn, website, official forms, references, and what the person confirmed). scripts/consistency_audit.py compares the sources. See method/CONSISTENCY.md.

truth_order.description: Source ids, most trusted first. Default: confirmed, official_form, references, cv, linkedin, website, then any others in file order.

organisation_aliases.description: Other names for the same organisation, for example a renamed employer: {"Fabrikam Air": ["Fabrikam Airlines"]}.

sources.description: One entry per source, keyed by a source id such as cv, linkedin, website, official_form, references or confirmed.

month.description: As the source shows it: 'Oct 2007', 'October 2007', '2007-10', '10/2007' or a year alone '2007'. 'present' for a current role. Null or missing means not given.

label.description: A short name for the report, for example 'CV (October 2026 version)'.

ref.description: Where the copy came from: a workspace path such as intake/sources/cv.pdf, or an address.

complete.description: True if this source should list every role in the period it covers. Default true for confirmed, official_form, cv and linkedin; false otherwise.

editable.description: False for records the person cannot change (a signed form, a referee's letter). Default false for official_form and references.

covers.description: The period the source asks about, for example an official form that asks for the last 10 years.

title.description: Exactly as the source writes it. Do not correct it while copying.

key.description: Optional. Records with the same key in different sources are the same role. Use it when the automatic match gets it wrong.

concurrent.description: True if this role really ran at the same time as another (for example a part-time board seat).

claims.description: Achievement lines from this source for this role, copied exactly.

denies.description: Usually on the confirmed source: things other sources say that the person says are not true.
